q: The legal principle by which the Clearing Corporation becomes the central counterparty to all trades is called:
e: Novation = substitution of a new party (the Clearing Corp) into a contract, replacing the original counterparties' bilateral exposure with exposure to the CC.

q: Which clearing corporation clears trades for NSE?
e: NCL (NSE Clearing Ltd) clears for NSE. ICCL clears for BSE; MCCIL for MSEI; CCIL for govt securities + money market.

q: Interoperability of clearing corporations was implemented in India in:
e: Implemented in 2019 (proposed 2018). Brokers can now clear and settle trades from any exchange through their preferred clearing corp.

q: T+1 settlement for cash equity in India:
e: Phased rollout completed in January 2023 — all NSE/BSE listed equity now settles on T+1. F&O has its own daily MTM cycle.

q: T+0 settlement, optional since 2024, has how many windows?
e: T+0 has 2 windows: Window 1 closes at 1:30 PM and Window 2 at 3:30 PM. Investor must voluntarily opt in for eligible stocks.

q: The minimum net worth required for a Clearing Member that clears for other Trading Members is:
e: ₹3 crore for a CM clearing for others (TCM/PCM). ₹1 crore for self-only (SCM). Plus ₹50 lakh deposit + ₹10 lakh per additional TM cleared.

q: Multilateral netting at the clearing corp:
o: Drastically reduces gross obligations to a single net per security
e: Multilateral netting nets all positions of all clients of a CM across the same security to a single net long or net short. Drastically cuts gross flow at settlement.

q: If a client has 10 lots long SBI on NSE and 6 lots short SBI on BSE with interoperability, the margin is computed on:
o: No margin since they offset perfectly
e: Interoperability nets across exchanges at the chosen clearing corp. Net = 4 lots long → margin on this. Capital efficiency benefit.

q: Pay-in / pay-out timing for cash equity on T+1 is approximately:
e: Pay-in (funds + securities) ~ 11 AM; pay-out (funds to seller, securities to buyer) ~ 1:30 PM on T+1. Settlement complete by EOD.

q: If a buyer fails to make pay-in, the clearing corp typically initiates:
e: Buyer's pay-in failure = monetary default. CC charges penalty and close-out (monetary settlement at exchange-determined price). Auction is for SELLER's failure to deliver securities.

o: Margin relief for hedged positions across cash + F&O
e: Cross-margin gives margin relief when positions hedge each other across cash and F&O segments. Recognises that the net economic risk is lower than gross.

q: On expiry, all in-the-money index options are:
o: Held over to the next month
e: ITM options auto-exercised by CC on expiry; cash settled at the difference between strike and closing spot. OTM expires worthless.

q: Position calculation at the CM rolls up:
o: TM proprietary nets + each client's net (clients NOT netted across each other)
All client positions netted across each other
e: TM proprietary nets per security; each client's positions are netted at client level (not across clients). CM rolls up TMs' totals per security per CC.

q: If a futures contract is not traded during the last 30 minutes of the day, the daily settlement price is:
o: Theoretical price using F = S × e^(r×t)
e: If untraded in the last 30 min, theoretical settlement = S × e^(r × t), where r is typically MIBOR or a specified rate.

q: The Settlement Guarantee Fund (SGF) is funded by:
o: CC contributions + member deposits + penalty collections
e: SGF funded by CC contributions + member deposits + penalty collections. Stress-tested monthly. Sized to meet 'extreme but plausible' default scenarios.

q: Daily settlement price for a futures contract is:
o: Last traded price of the futures contract
Volume-weighted average price of the last 30 minutes of futures trading
e: Daily settlement price uses the volume-weighted average of the last 30 min of futures trading. If untraded, theoretical price F = S × e^(r × t).

q: When a member defaults, the resources used after the defaulter's collateral are (in order):
e: Cascade: Defaulter's margins/collateral → SGF → CC's own capital (mandatory minimum) → Surviving members' contributions. Always defaulter pays first.

q: A Clearing Member must have at least how much initial deposit with the CC?
e: ₹50 lakh initial deposit with the CC at induction. Plus ₹10 lakh additional per extra TM cleared. Maintained as part of liquid assets.
